newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rye offered into German intervention stores.
newsitem.headline: Rye offered into German intervention stores.

text.p: Rye dominated German grain offers into public stores last week, with 13,150 tonnes earmarked for intervention, the state board BLE said on Monday.
Offers of other cereals were slim, reflecting firm free market prices and thinning supply at the end of the old crop season, traders said.
Total grain volumes offered in the November-May 1996/97 intervention season lag those of last year.
By May 2, a total 1,071,208 tonnes had been offered compared with 1,661,311 tonnes a year earlier, BLE figures showed.
The May buying-in price for all grains has been set at 247.98 marks/tonne.
